title: Achieving High-Performance Fault-Tolerant Routing in HyperX Interconnection Networks
problem: HyperX networks require routing mechanisms that simultaneously balance traffic and tolerate failures, but standard algorithms lack deadlock-free paths when link or node failures occur in low-diameter topologies.
motivation: HyperX topologies are cost-competitive alternatives to Fat Trees, but only if sophisticated routing maintains performance and reliability under frequent hardware failures.
method: SurePath leverages standard routing algorithms enhanced with an Up/Down escape subnetwork for deadlock avoidance. When failures occur, packets route through the escape subnetwork while maintaining deadlock-free guarantees via hierarchical routing, enabling fault-tolerant packet delivery.
key_novelty: Combining standard routing with an Up/Down escape subnetwork to achieve simultaneous deadlock avoidance and fault tolerance in HyperX topologies.
contributions: SurePath: fault-tolerant routing algorithm for HyperX interconnection networks
Up/Down escape subnetwork-based deadlock avoidance mechanism for faulty topologies
Evaluation demonstrating no performance degradation across traffic patterns under high failure rates

metrics.other: throughput and latency maintained under faulty scenarios; no performance degradation across traffic patterns

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
